text:
ravi: throwing this out for discussion: what if we switch from passive demote to a lease-token model for residency? tenants get short-lived lease tokens for pages; tokens carry priority and expiry and can be preempted with graceful drain. goal: predictable backpressure, easier accounting, better fairness.

mona: interesting. tokens = lightweight objects tracked per-page + tenant? how do we avoid token explosion?

ravi: tokens are compact (tenant_id, score, expire_ts) and we only allocate on promote. common-case stays tokenless. think of it as a soft reservation that decays if not refreshed.

kevin: how does preemption work? sudden preempt kills in-flight inferences. we need a graceful reclaim handshake.

zara: proposal: two-phase preempt. 1) send PREEMPT_NOTICE with drain_deadline (e.g., 250ms). 2) if still occupied after deadline, force demote but attempt to keep KV cache snapshot for faster re-warm on re-promote.

mona: nice. also add token.priority (0..3). scheduler uses priority + age to pick victims. high-priority tokens harder to preempt. we should cap per-tenant high-priority tokens.

kevin: tenant fairness: what if a tenant spins up many short jobs to hoard tokens? need leak-based credit and cooldown. maybe require a renewal rate and reject renewals when tenant_credit exhausted.

ravi: yes: tenant_credit refills at X tokens/sec and renewals consume credit. renewals beyond credit get backoff or are assigned lower priority.

zara: API surface: runtime will expose `page.acquire_lease(tenant, priority, ttl_ms)` and `page.renew_lease(tenant, lease_id)` and `page.release_lease(lease_id)`. model runners can use hints: `buf.lease_hint(priority=1|2|3, ttl=ms)`.

kevin: what about streaming/scans? they shouldn't get long leases. streaming detector auto-assigns priority=0 and ttl small (50-100ms).

mona: telemetry: `leases.active_count`, `leases.preempted_count`, `tenant.lease_credit`, `lease.handoff_latency_ms`, `lease.forced_demote_rate`, `lease.rewarm_hit_rate`. dashboards to correlate with p99 latency and eviction churn.

ravi: compaction interplay: when we preempt a block of leases, we may create a compaction opportunity. emit `compaction_candidate` with estimated benefit. but avoid compacting while many leases are short-lived. add hysteresis.

kevin: safety: must be able to instantly disable leases in emergency. feature flag `mem.lease.enabled=false` and `mem.lease.preempt_grace_ms=0` to force immediate demote.

zara: rollout plan: stage 1 - simulation harness + unit tests for fairness and handoff. stage 2 - canary 5% tenants with non-critical models (dedicated dev pool). stage 3 - 25% with telemetry gating. metrics to watch: reclaim success rate, rewarm hit, p99 latency, and tail cost.

mona: test harness should simulate mixed workloads: hot-spot churn, long streams, multi-tenant bursts. include adversarial tenant trying to game renewal.

ravi: thought: add a short token log to help debugging: `lease.trace=<tenant,lease_id,event>` for last N events per node. minimal perf cost.

deploy-bot: experiment created: `mem.lease.enabled=true`, `lease.default_ttl_ms=1000`, `lease.preempt_grace_ms=250`, rollout=5% tenants.

kevin: one more: when we preempt, try opportunistic snapshot to host (delta-compressed) so re-promote cost lower. if snapshot too expensive, skip. heuristic: snapshot when page.dirty == false && page.last_promote_cost > threshold.

zara: good. I'll draft RFC addendum with token schema, APIs, telemetry, knobs, and a small state machine for acquire/renew/preempt. assign to @zara.

mona: :thumbsup: assign to @mona for simulation harness.

ravi: thanks all. will open ENG-RUNTIME-8102 for the RFC + simulation tasks.

deploy-bot: task ENG-RUNTIME-8102 created and assigned->zara,mona.
